messages:
alice: deploy-bot failed to promote release v1.8.3 -> staging. CI shows artifact fetch error, checksum mismatch. tagging hold for now. https://ci.redwood.internal/teams/release/12345 :eyes:
deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion job #4567 FAILED. error=artifact_check_sum_mismatch expected=sha256:3a7f... got=sha256:9f2b... See /artifacts/2026/03/20/v1.8.3/* for uploads.
ben: ack. Is this coming from our s3 cache or the registry mirror?
carla: looks like remote-cache restore failed in the build logs. there's a `restore-artifacts` step that returned a 200 but the blob content differs. possible partial upload or storage dedupe anomaly.
devops-oncall: sharing `gsutil` check we ran earlier: `gsutil hash gs://redwood-artifacts/2026/03/20/v1.8.3.tar.gz` returned "Hash (crc32c): 1a2b3c, MD5: 9f2b..." which matches the CI-observed value (9f2b...). expected in manifest was 3a7f...
alice: so manifest (generated at build) had checksum 3a7f... but object now is 9f2b... suggests either build wrote wrong object or object was rewritten after manifest creation. who wrote the object?
carla: builder step uses `upload-artifact` which does a multipart upload to the storage gateway. there were some warnings about timeouts in the uploader earlier in the logs. could be a retry that concatenated or truncated parts?
ben: any chance the dedupe/compose job on the storage side replaced the object with a different version but same name? we had that bug in 2025. rolling back storage autoscaler recently.
devops-oncall: checking storage audit: "2026-03-20T14:12:03 uploader@ci-service PUT /2026/03/20/v1.8.3.tar.gz etag=9f2b..." and earlier "2026-03-20T14:11:58 builder@local PUT /2026/03/20/v1.8.3.tar.gz etag=3a7f..." So two puts within ~5s. second overwrote the first. need to see why duplicate names used.
maya: quick ask: is this blocking the staging promotion? we should decide whether to abort and pin to v1.8.2 or attempt to repush v1.8.3 artifact now.
alice: blocking. deploy-bot won't promote with checksum mismatch. my vote: hold promotion, replicate correct artifact from build worker (if available) or republish, then re-run the promotion. if not quick, revert to last known-good (v1.8.2) for staging and continue release window later.
carla: we can try to fetch the original artifact from the builder node if it still exists in /tmp or the build cache. pinging @ben to see if the builder is still alive for that run.
ben: builder vm drained after pipeline. we have the raw tar in remote cache snapshot `cache-snap-2026-03-20-14` but snapshot restore is slow. alternative: re-run the exact build with `--no-cache` to regenerate artifact and verify checksum then upload.
devops-oncall: temporary mitigation: we can lock the storage object naming to include `build-id` to avoid overwrites, but that requires patch and a new deploy. not today. For immediate: I'll run a consistency flush on the artifact path and re-run a single upload from CI (manual) to replace the bad blob with the known-good one if we can find it.
alice: please do a quick audit first so we don't overwrite the correct one. we need an action plan and ETA.
devops-oncall: running audit now. command I ran: ``gsutil ls -l gs://redwood-artifacts/2026/03/20/ && gsutil stat gs://redwood-artifacts/2026/03/20/v1.8.3.tar.gz`` found two versions in logs but storage only shows latest. also kicking off `restore-snapshot cache-snap-2026-03-20-14 --path v1.8.3.tar.gz` (no ETA, could be ~20m).
carla: if snapshot comes back, we can compute its checksum and if matches manifest, repromote. otherwise re-run build.
maya: decision: hold promotion to staging for v1.8.3. create a hotfix task: RH-789 (assign devops-oncall + carla). re-run build with `--no-cache` if snapshot doesn't yield a match by +30m. pin staging to v1.8.2 for now. schedule a follow-up in next 60m to confirm.
ben: I'll open a PR to promote v1.8.2 -> staging so downstream QA isn't blocked.
devops-oncall: snapshot restore started 14:26:10, estimated 18 minutes. I'll post results.
alice: thanks. can someone also check artifact indexer and cache invalidation so future uses of the stale key don't pick up the wrong blob?
carla: noted, adding indexer flush to RH-789.
devops-oncall: update: snapshot restore finished 14:44:25. `sha256(snapshot-v1.8.3.tar.gz)=3a7f...` which matches manifest. I'm going to upload that as `v1.8.3-recovered-2026-03-20.tar.gz` and then we can run a promote test.
alice: yes please upload with a new name and test promote to a non-critical staging namespace first.
maya: if promote test passes, we can decide to proceed with v1.8.3 or still prefer v1.8.2 for today. we'll sync with QA.
ben: promote test started. deploy-bot responded: [automated] dry-run promote ok for v1.8.3-recovered-2026-03-20.
alice: great. QA wants more time for smoke tests; recommend we keep staging pinned to v1.8.2 for the change window and schedule v1.8.3 for the next one.
maya: agreed. final: hold v1.8.3 promotion, promote v1.8.2 -> staging now (PR by ben), mark RH-789 for postmortem, and add a follow-up to include unique artifact names to avoid overwrite race. closing thread after actions done. :white_check_mark:
ben: PR merged, staging set to v1.8.2.
devops-oncall: RH-789 created and assigned. I'll include audit logs and the snapshot steps in the ticket. :memo:
carla: thanks team.
maya: thanks, closing out for now. :shipit:
